page.headline: Does rsync beat xs on real trees and edge cases?
page.intro: The lab is testing how fast three file-transfer tools reach durable storage: rsync, xs-c++ and xs-rs. Today's schedule has a single runner, the Mac to apollo link. The first experiment, on the user's real csearchv3 tree, is running now, and the remaining edge-case tests queue behind it.

runners.title: Mac ↔ apollo: mars's box on Linux

items.asks: On the user's csearchv3 tree (14 GB, 1,345,908 files, 472,330 directories), rsync -a, xs-c++ -a -j4 and xs-rs -a -j4 differ by more than 5% in time to durable in some cell.
items.hypothesis: On the user's csearchv3 tree (14 GB, 1,345,908 files, 472,330 directories), rsync -a, xs-c++ -a -j4 and xs-rs -a -j4 differ by more than 5% in time to durable in some cell.
items.why: Running now on the user's real csearchv3 tree, it checks whether the three tools differ by over 5% in time to durable, which matters for this user's own workload.

items.asks: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. Delta updates of large files: a 4 KiB edit in a file (update-1pct), and a file grown at its end (append-1pct).
items.hypothesis: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. Delta updates of large files: a 4 KiB edit in a file (update-1pct), and a file grown at its end (append-1pct).
items.why: It tests whether rsync's delta updates beat the xs tools when large files get a small edit or grow at the end, a common real-world pattern.

items.asks: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. No-ops with --checksum, where every file is read and hashed at both ends. xs-rs has no -c, so it sits out.
items.hypothesis: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. No-ops with --checksum, where every file is read and hashed at both ends. xs-rs has no -c, so it sits out.
items.why: With --checksum, every file is read and hashed at both ends, so it tests rsync's verification cost on unchanged data. xs-rs sits out because it has no -c.

items.asks: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. No-ops of many files, where NT1021 saw rsync pull real-psample in 75.7 s against xs-cpp 151.6 s; -j1 arms for a per-core comparison.
items.hypothesis: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. No-ops of many files, where NT1021 saw rsync pull real-psample in 75.7 s against xs-cpp 151.6 s; -j1 arms for a per-core comparison.
items.why: An earlier run had rsync pulling real-psample in 75.7 s against 151.6 s for xs-cpp, so this checks that gap on many no-op files, with -j1 arms for per-core comparison.

items.asks: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. Fresh copies of 1 MiB and 16 MiB files and of mixed-threshold, around xs's whole-file and split thresholds; -j1 arms as in RW3.
items.hypothesis: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. Fresh copies of 1 MiB and 16 MiB files and of mixed-threshold, around xs's whole-file and split thresholds; -j1 arms as in RW3.
items.why: Fresh copies of 1 MiB and 16 MiB files, plus mixed sizes, probe behaviour around xs's whole-file and split thresholds.

items.asks: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. A backup whose source lost 10% of its files: --delete must remove them. xs-rs has no --delete, so it sits out.
items.hypothesis: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. A backup whose source lost 10% of its files: --delete must remove them. xs-rs has no --delete, so it sits out.
items.why: A backup whose source lost 10% of its files tests whether --delete removes them at the destination. xs-rs sits out because it has no --delete.

items.asks: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. Hard links kept with -H, on laikav2 (1,234 linked files in its Rust target folder). xs-rs has no -H, so it sits out.
items.hypothesis: rsync is at least 5% faster to durable than xs-c++ or xs-rs in some cell. Hard links kept with -H, on laikav2 (1,234 linked files in its Rust target folder). xs-rs has no -H, so it sits out.
items.why: It checks whether rsync -H keeps the 1,234 hard-linked files in laikav2's Rust target folder intact. xs-rs sits out because it has no -H.
